model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect sizes for various language families and isolated languages, comparing the performance of different models across these categories. The horizontal axis displays the language families (IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic) and the vertical axis represents the effect size, with values ranging from approximately -5 to 35. Each category has a group of bars representing different models: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (medium green), mBERT-B2 (light pink), and XLM-B2 (dark pink). Error bars are shown for each bar, indicating variability. The chart shows that the IE-Indic family has the highest effect sizes for all models, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 23. The IE-Germanic family also shows relatively high effect sizes, particularly for XLM-L2 and XLM-B2, both around 15. In contrast, the Isolate and Uralic categories have much lower effect sizes, generally below 5. The mBERT-L2 and XLM-L2 models tend to have lower effect sizes compared to their B2 counterparts across most categories. The Semitic family shows a notable peak for XLM-L2, with an effect size around 18, while the mBERT-L2 model has a negative effect size in this category.
